I will keep a straightforward winter wheat and summer maize rotation on the same land. In Quzhou County, that is still the most dependable way for me to use the full year, match the local climate, and protect my income. I am 60, educated, and I would rather run a system that is proven, efficient, and easy to manage precisely than chase novelty. Winter wheat fits the cool season well, and summer maize follows naturally after wheat harvest. That gives me two harvests from the same fields and spreads risk better than putting everything into one crop.

I will use improved seed for wheat and hybrid seed for maize. For wheat, I want stable tillering, disease tolerance, and good grain quality. For maize, I want strong stand establishment, heat tolerance, and high yield potential. I will not push fertilizer blindly. I would apply enough nitrogen to support yield, keep phosphorus steady for rooting and grain formation, and add potassium because it helps stress tolerance and stand strength. I would also control irrigation carefully. Water matters in Hebei, so I would irrigate wheat at the key stages and keep maize irrigation limited but timely, especially around jointing and grain filling if rainfall is short.

I will manage weeds, insects, and diseases with a moderate number of pesticide applications instead of spraying by habit. Wheat will usually need fewer sprays unless disease pressure rises; maize will need attention to borers, armyworm, and leaf disease depending on the season. For tillage, I would use rotary tillage because it is practical for residue handling and seedbed preparation in this rotation. My goal is not the maximum theoretical yield. My goal is stable, repeatable production with controlled costs, efficient field operations, and acceptable risk.
